transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-12-04 14:30 UTC | Duration: 58m | Attendees: Maya, Ravi, Claire, Jordan - Redwood; Evan, Nadia, Drew, Liam - SummitEdge

Summary (auto): quick sprint to align pipeline priorities for the NorthStar co-sell program, identify blockers for two high-priority accounts, and confirm next steps for security docs and exec intro.

[00:00] Maya Ortiz: ok everyone, thanks for jumping on. we're trying to keep this as a sprint style triage, uh, two big deals today — AcmeCloud and Meridian Health — and then any blockers. gonna kick it to Evan for quick alignment from SummitEdge side.
[00:18] Evan Torres: hey all, thanks Maya. yes, quick context — our account owners at Acme are asking for a sandbox demo with private model hosting; Meridian is more compliance sensitive, data residency + HIPAA-ish, so we need to map how Redwood Private would look, and what the timeline is.
[00:36] Ravi Patel: cool. technical quick note — for private deployment there are two flavors: VPC-hosted control plane with customer-managed keys, or fully air-gapped on-prem. both have different onboarding windows. typically VPC path is 2-4 weeks to stand up; on-prem is more like 6-10 weeks depending on infra.
[00:56] Nadia Kim: okay good, that helps. for Meridian specifically they need SOC2 plus an audit trail and HSM-backed KMS, is that supported? I know Redwood mentioned KMS integrations earlier but want to confirm.
[01:14] Claire Zhang: yes we have KMS integrations — we support AWS KMS and customer HSM via standard key wrapping, though for air-gapped there are extra manual steps. audit logs and per-token tracing are available in the console; we'll share the compliance appendix.
[01:32] Drew Patel: can you share the appendix today? we need to push to our legal by Friday.
[01:38] Maya Ortiz: we'll put the appendix in the shared drive after this call. link in notes. Claire will own the compliance doc upload.
[01:46] Jordan Lee: just to add, from the co-sell play perspective, revenue share for these pilots is flexible; we usually do a first-90-day discount plus partner uplift on renewals. but we need to align on deal roles: who owns renewal commit, who is the customer POC.
[02:05] Evan Torres: SummitEdge will own primary customer relationship for both; Redwood should be listed as technical provider with a joint account exec for escalation.
[02:14] Maya Ortiz: great, sounds good. let's walk through AcmeCloud scope first.

-- AcmeCloud (opportunity deep-dive) --
[02:26] Maya Ortiz: AcmeCloud wants a low-latency LLM endpoint embedded into their customer dashboard. key asks: 50ms p50 for single-tenant endpoint, cost target sub-$0.0008 per token, and SSO integration with their Okta.
[02:45] Ravi Patel: 50ms p50 is aggressive depending on seq length and model; if they're using a 2k context it may be doable with tuned batching, but we should propose two options: hosted low-latency SKU or dedicated reserved GPU pool. dedicated gives more predictable latency.
[03:03] Evan Torres: what's the delta in monthly committed spend between those?
[03:08] Jordan Lee: rough numbers: hosted — pay-as-you-go, likely variable cost; dedicated — expect a monthly commit starting ~$40k for the footprint they want. can put a better estimate after Ravi's infra T-shirt.
[03:20] Drew Patel: Acme is sensitive to vendor lock-in — they asked about model portability and ability to run on-prem later.
[03:28] Claire Zhang: portability is in our thesis — same API surface across hosted, dedicated, private. migration requires a one-time model transfer step and potentially re-quantization for different hardware. we'll note caveats.
[03:41] Evan Torres: perfect. next, Meridian Health.

-- Meridian Health (compliance-heavy) --
[03:52] Nadia Kim: Meridian will only consider options that keep data in-region and an auditable key lifecycle. also they asked whether Redwood stores any PII in logs, and retention windows.
[04:05] Claire Zhang: we can configure zero retention for requests and enable customer-managed keys; audit logs can be exported to their SIEM. retention defaults to 30 days but can be set to 0 for certain contracts. I'll include a sample retention config.
[04:20] Liam O'Connor: how does fallback routing work if a dedicated pool is saturated? won't want to send PHI to other models.
[04:27] Ravi Patel: fallback is policy-driven; for PHI you'd configure strict fallback to compatible private variants only, never to hosted multi-tenant. that requires capacity reservations or burst slots.
[04:38] Evan Torres: ok that might be a blocker if costs spike. we need a clear runbook and cost guardrails.
[04:45] Maya Ortiz: we'll put those guardrails into the joint account plan with explicit SLOs and overspend alerts.

-- Pipeline & Prioritization --
[04:58] Maya Ortiz: looking at our joint pipeline sheet — three live opportunities in NorthStar but we want to prioritize Acme and Meridian for Q1 pilot. criteria: probability, technical readiness, legal/security checklist completion, and potential ARR.
[05:16] Drew Patel: can we map owners? I'd propose: Acme — Evan / Maya as AE pair; Meridian — Nadia / Jordan. Redwood SEs would be Ravi for Acme, Claire for Meridian.
[05:27] Evan Torres: agreed.
[05:30] Nadia Kim: timeline check — if we start the compliance review now and exchange SOC2 docs by next week, can Redwood commit to a pilot kickoff mid-Jan?
[05:40] Ravi Patel: mid-Jan for VPC private pilot seems plausible; depends on infra booking. for on-prem it's unlikely.
[05:49] Maya Ortiz: ok mid-Jan target — we'll aim for executive intro week of 2025-12-15 to lock stakeholders, then security exchange, then kickoff planning workshop w/ SEs first week of Jan.

[06:05] Jordan Lee: on commercialization, we should finalize pricing bands so SummitEdge can present to procurement. I'll draft two tiers: pilot discounted, then standard co-sell split on renewal.
[06:18] Evan Torres: what about competitive positioning — companies asked about Anthropic and HF's enterprise features, how do we position Redwood?
[06:27] Maya Ortiz: emphasize predictable inference economics, unified runtime across modes, and observability — token-level cost and per-route latency. customers value that when they run production workloads. also mention our rollout fallback and quantization recommendations to cut cost.
[06:43] Nadia Kim: procurement may also ask about marketplace listings and third-party attestations. have you seen procurement pushback in that area?
[06:51] Claire Zhang: we have marketplace listings with major clouds and can share attestation artifacts. will include a short pack.

-- Risk triage & blockers --
[07:05] Maya Ortiz: list of current blockers: SOC2 snapshot pending, Meridian's region constraint (EU-only), Acme's low-latency SLO + cost cap, and exec alignment. which of these are highest risk?
[07:18] Drew Patel: Meridian region + SOC2 is high risk; Acme's cost is medium but solvable. exec alignment is medium.
[07:25] Maya Ortiz: ok priority order noted.

[07:32] Evan Torres: one more technical Q — are there limits on model versions we can run in dedicated pools? Acme wants a bleeding-edge open model.
[07:40] Ravi Patel: we onboard models into our catalog; bleeding-edge models often need extra tuning and validation. dedicated pools can run custom models but there is an onboarding window for kernel selection and perf profiling. estimate 2-3 weeks if it's similar arch, longer if it's entirely new.
[07:58] Nadia Kim: if performance regresses after rollout how do you handle rollbacks?
[08:03] Claire Zhang: we support canary and automatic fallback policies; we also tie quality monitoring to prompt sets so we can detect regression and rollback to last verified model.
[08:14] Evan Torres: good.

-- Close & Recap --
[08:20] Maya Ortiz: recap: 1) Redwood to upload compliance appendix and joint account plan draft by 2025-12-08; 2) SummitEdge to send SOC2 snapshot and regional constraints by 2025-12-10; 3) set exec intro week of 2025-12-15; 4) SEs to prepare pilot infra T-shirt estimates by 2025-12-09.
[08:41] Nadia Kim: yep that's aligned.
[08:45] Maya Ortiz: any final questions?
[08:48] Liam O'Connor: small note — please redact any vendor telemetry in the docs we share; our legal is sensitive to third-party telemetry.
[08:55] Claire Zhang: noted. we'll scrub and provide a sanitized appendix.
[09:00] Maya Ortiz: perfect. thanks everyone — we'll follow up in the shared folder.

(Transcript continues with brief Q&A and off-topic scheduling chatter; some segments auto-summarized.)

[10:30] Evan Torres: quick logistics — can we get a 30-min deep dive with Meridian's security team next week?
[10:37] Maya Ortiz: yes. I'll loop in our security eng and schedule via calendar.

[11:05] Nadia Kim: thanks all.

End meeting.

References shared: joint-account-plan-draft.docx (link placeholder), compliance-appendix.pdf (link placeholder), pipeline-spreadsheet (link placeholder)
